about: Machine-checkable constants and cases for docs/contracts/universe-repo-open-v1.md.
Only the lead changes this file. Any change bumps contractVersion and the pinned sha256 (README-universe-repo-open.md).
Consumers commit a byte-identical copy and assert its sha256; they never restate a value from here without a test that compares it to this file.
No secret values. The only real Auth0 client ids here are the two production ones, listed so staging code can refuse them.
Regex sources are JavaScript syntax with no flags. PHP consumers anchor with \A and \z (PHP $ also matches before a final newline); Python consumers use re.fullmatch.
Grant-shaped strings are never written literally. Expand ${repeat:<char>:<count>} before use (see expansion).

expansion.rule: Replace every occurrence with <character> repeated <count> times, left to right, before any other use of the string.

regexRelationsRule: equal: identical source and predicate set. subset: checked structurally, not by sampling. Each row has exactly one os-grant class: STAGING the 1.0.3 legacy grant (no class key), QA project, DEFAULT none (os routes unmounted, production unchanged). A pin is effective only if it is not UNPINNED, not empty and not in PRODUCTION_AUTH0_CLIENTS; at Works only, the OS pin is also ineffective when it equals the Universe pin. createServer mounts the os routes (osPaths) only when deployment.osClient !== null; otherwise their paths are unmatched for every request, including act-as requests.

authRule: 0. Mounting: createServer drops the two os routes from the mounted selfserve module when deployment.osClient === null (a path filter over the declared module; manifest.ts unchanged). Their paths are then undeclared for every request, whatever the bearer or act-as header, and each request gets exactly what an undeclared /v1 path answers for it today, byte-identical to 7974ab6c: 404 unmatched_route for a bearer the /v1 middleware accepts (a production EZiL ID client without act-as, or a Supabase bearer with or without act-as); otherwise the middleware's own refusal, which precedes routing: 401 identity_token_invalid for an EZiL ID client outside v1Clients (on DEFAULT: OS-staging and Universe-staging), and 403 ezil_id_delegation_forbidden for an accepted EZiL ID bearer with an act-as header.
1. EZiL ID bearer: verify with acceptedClients = deployment.v1Clients; verifyEzilIdToken returns the matched client. Failure: 401 identity_token_invalid (unchanged middleware).

2. Middleware, centrally, immediately after verifyEzilIdToken returns and before resolveEzilIdAccount: a token whose matched client is deployment.osClient on any path that is not an os path: 401 identity_token_invalid. No GoTrue admin call is made for such a request.
3. Then the unchanged middleware: account resolution, account_suspended, ezil_id_builders_only, and an act-as header with an EZiL ID bearer: 403 ezil_id_delegation_forbidden.

4. A Supabase bearer passes the middleware as today. On a mounted os route, an act-as header reaches delegatedRequest first (403 act_as_operator_required for a non-operator); without one, the os handler refuses it because it carries no matched client: 401 identity_token_invalid.
5. os handlers: matched client !== osClient: 401 identity_token_invalid. (deployment.osClient === null cannot reach a handler; the handler also returns c.notFound() if it ever does.)
6. os-grant accepts only a lowercase UUID ref (any other ref: 404 not_found). Every other self-serve route keeps the numeric ref only (NUMERIC_REF_RE with int64_max), on every deployment.

osGrantRequest.classRule: 1.0.5. valid/invalid above are the STAGING (legacy, 1.0.3) row and are unchanged except one added invalid case: a class key is refused there, as it always was (strict body). project lists the QA row: the body must be exactly {computerLabel, class: 'project'}; anything else, a missing class included, is 422 invalid_request. The class a row grants is the server's (WORKS_OS_GRANT_CLASSES), never chosen by the caller: the body must name it explicitly and is refused when it does not match. Authentication (works.authRule) runs before the body is read, so a wrong-audience token is 401 whatever the body.

osSession.rule: In one transaction: lock the account row (select ... for update), find a live row with device_label 'ezil-os '+label, os 'ezil-os', cli_version 'os-repo-v1', access_hash null, revoked_at null and expires_at > now + OS_SESSION_MIN_REMAINING_MS; else insert one with expires_at = now + OS_SESSION_TTL_MS. Never update expires_at.

works.osGrantProjectRule: 1.0.5 (Works W2/W3 T3). On the QA row, POST /v1/builder/selfserve-repositories/:repositoryRef/os-grant with body {computerLabel, class: 'project'} issues the project grant: authentication, ref, ownership (ownedByRepositoryId), preconditions (osGrantPreconditions), the session row (osSession: one per account and computerLabel, the same row any class uses) and scope (authority.scope) exactly as the legacy grant; webClone false; routePath exactly <handle>/<name>.git. Only the expiry differs: expiresAt = min(issuedAt + PROJECT_GRANT_TTL_MS, the bearer's exp), never later (osGrantProjectExpiry), which fits git_grants_expiry_chk unchanged (no schema change). The answer is the legacy keys plus class: 'project' (osGrantProjectResponse), cloneUrl on the row's gitHost. os-sessions/revoke revokes the label's session and so every grant of either class (works.osRevokeRequest, gitAuthorize grant_revoked / session_revoked); an expired grant is grant_expired. The gateway does not know the class and needs none: the expiry and the route path carry it. The 60-minute web-clone grant (clone-token, webClone true) is unchanged and is never a project grant: every project consumer refuses expiresAt beyond PROJECT_GRANT_ACCEPT_MAX_MS and a missing or other class.

osGrantProjectExpiry.rule: expiresAt = min(issuedAt + PROJECT_GRANT_TTL_MS, bearerExp). bearerExp is the exp the token verifier itself verified, carried through the /v1 middleware to this route, never read from the body. The verifier's legacy clock tolerance (up to 60 s past exp) does not reach issuance: bearerExp <= issuedAt is 401 identity_token_invalid BEFORE any session row or grant is written, so no grant is ever non-positive. Other routes keep their verification unchanged.

cases.note: inside the verifier's legacy 60 s tolerance: accepted by authentication, refused by issuance

projectGrantRenewal.rule: Consumer (the OS app/shell, through Universe open and the Worker repo-grant route). Renewal is scheduled from the expiresAt actually returned, never from a fixed timer and never from the legacy REFRESH_LEAD_MS rule. With remaining = expiresAt - now on receipt: (a) remaining < PROJECT_GRANT_MIN_INSTALL_MS: not installed (the Worker refuses it too); reauthenticate the EZiL ID (silent, prompt=none) once, then ask again; (b) remaining <= PROJECT_RENEW_LEAD_MS: installed, but the bearer limited it, so the next renewal first reauthenticates once, then asks (asking again at once would return the same short grant, so there is no loop); (c) otherwise installed and renewed at expiresAt - PROJECT_RENEW_LEAD_MS. At most one renewal in flight per (computer, repository). A failed reauthentication or a 401/403 stops renewal and shows sign in again, leaving the folder, uncommitted work and HEAD untouched. A revoked session is never extended or revived: the next grant comes from a new session row (osSession).

osGrantProjectResponse.consumerRule: A project consumer (Universe's builder open, which answers OS; and through it the OS Worker repo-open/repo-grant, the AWS relay, host and kernel) accepts exactly these keys, class === 'project', cloneUrl on the route's project host (on os-staging git-qa.ezil.work), the requested repositoryId, and expiresAt in (now, now + PROJECT_GRANT_ACCEPT_MAX_MS]: PROJECT_GRANT_TTL_MS plus PROJECT_GRANT_SKEW_MS of clock skew. Universe additionally caps it at the userIdToken's exp + 30 s (os-builder-project-open-v1 universeOpen.grant). A legacy consumer refuses a class key (osGrantResponse).

workerRequest.projectRule: 1.0.4. class project: an ordinary Builder-created project's own repository on the Creator's own computer (never a new or assessment computer). It is the third member of REPO_OPEN_CLASSES and has no entry in REPO_OPEN_CLASS_GIT_HOSTS (the single-host table): its gitHost must be one of REPO_OPEN_PROJECT_GIT_HOSTS AND exactly the host the ROUTE's deployment serves (the route passes it: github.ezil.work in production, git-qa.ezil.work on os-staging; GIT_PRODUCTION_HOST stays forbidden on staging), so a body never chooses its host. The AWS host op and the kernel cannot know the deployment and accept either project host; the route binding is the Worker's (invalidMutations rows with layer worker are refused by the Worker only, every other row at every layer). path must be null (its editor root is always the wrapper W, kernel.project.layoutRule). The grant's expiresAt must be in (now, now + projectGrantMaxMs]: an OS-scoped grant of at most five minutes plus 30 s skew, never the 60-minute Works web-clone grant (cli-auth issueGrant webClone). 1.0.5: that grant is Works os-grant with class 'project' on the QA row (works.osGrantProjectRule), issued for at most PROJECT_GRANT_TTL_MS; projectGrantMaxMs equals PROJECT_GRANT_ACCEPT_MAX_MS. A project route also requires the deployment's capability and assessment-fence gates (awsProject) before anything is sent. A project body is refused on the personal and assessment routes, and a personal or assessment body on the project route (Worker invalid_request; AWS host repo_open_invalid; kernel workspace_failed).
workerRequest.classRule: 1.0.3. A body may carry one more key, class: personal or assessment (constants REPO_OPEN_CLASSES); absent means REPO_OPEN_CLASS_DEFAULT (personal), so every 1.0.2 body is valid and unchanged. class must be a string in REPO_OPEN_CLASSES (null, empty and any other value are invalid). gitHost must equal REPO_OPEN_CLASS_GIT_HOSTS[class]: a closed table, refused in both directions (personal or absent on git-qa, assessment on git-preview). gitHostAllowList is the class-absent (personal) list. Whoever relays the body (Worker, AWS host) forwards class into the kernel request (kernel.optionalRequestKeys) only when the body carried it. E1-6: a body with class assessment must carry path null (its editor root is always the wrapper, kernel.assessment.layoutRule); a non-null path is refused at every layer (Worker invalid_request, AWS host repo_open_invalid, kernel workspace_failed). repositoryId is the lowercase UUID the wrapper is named after.

URLSearchParams.set semantics (one value, first position kept). Applied to every navigation of a minted URL in a window that has ctx.project.

repoBudget.rule: Bytes are tar bytes, as the codec's PAX_FORMAT archive will spend them (worker/src/workspace-snapshot-script.ts:159,173,179), never raw file bytes. entryTarBytes = TAR_BLOCK_BYTES + (regular file ? TAR_BLOCK_BYTES * ceil(size / TAR_BLOCK_BYTES) : 0) + pax, where pax = 0 unless the entry name or symlink target is TAR_PAX_NAME_BYTES or more UTF-8 bytes, or not ASCII; then pax = TAR_BLOCK_BYTES + TAR_BLOCK_BYTES * ceil((nameBytes + linkBytes + TAR_PAX_RECORD_SLACK_BYTES) / TAR_BLOCK_BYTES). Directory and symlink sizes count 0. The workspace side counts exactly the entries the codec would archive (workspaceRule, 1.0.2; before 1.0.2 it counted every entry, so one untracked dependency install refused every open). The staged side is measured under its final names (REPO_DIR_TEMPLATE + '/' + relative path, the folder itself included), plus one directory entry for each of repos and repos/<handle> that does not exist yet (class assessment, 1.0.3 E1-6: ASSESSMENT_DIR_TEMPLATE + '/' + ASSESSMENT_CLONE_DIR_NAME + '/' + relative path, plus projects and projects/<repositoryId> when absent). Refuse with repository_too_large unless workspaceTarBytes + stagedTarBytes + TAR_ARCHIVE_TAIL_BYTES <= floor(SNAPSHOT_LIMIT_BYTES * REPO_BUDGET_FRACTION) AND workspaceEntries + stagedEntries <= floor(SNAPSHOT_MAX_ENTRIES * REPO_BUDGET_FRACTION). The workspace scan stops as soon as either sum is over.
repoBudget.tailNote: TAR_ARCHIVE_TAIL_BYTES = two end-of-archive blocks (1024) plus the worst-case padding to tarfile's 10240-byte record (10240). The codec's final check is os.path.getsize(path) <= LIMIT, which includes both.
repoBudget.concurrency: At most one op 'open' runs per sandbox (Worker in-flight map, contract section 8 step 5), so at most one staged clone is ever counted against the budget. User activity can still cross 100% (contract section 19).
repoBudget.workspaceRule: 1.0.2, tracked 1.0.3 codec parity. The workspace side applies the snapshot codec's own skip rules (worker/src/workspace-snapshot-script.ts inventory()), in the codec's order, to every entry under the root; a skipped directory's whole subtree is skipped. (1) A top-level name in SNAPSHOT_INTERNAL_NAMES, or the top-level STAGING_ROOT_NAME node. (2) Outside a .git path (no path component equal to .git): an entry whose own name is in SNAPSHOT_CACHE_NAMES (file, directory or symlink) unless its path is in tracked; a name containing a backslash; anything but a regular file, directory or symlink (FIFOs, sockets, devices); a symlink whose target is empty, absolute or contains a backslash, whose normalised dirname(name)/target is '..' or starts with '../', or whose realpath leaves the root. Inside a .git path nothing is skipped. tracked is built exactly as the codec builds it (1.0.3 codec parity: OS codec 463d1543, script sha256 58920eaa3e346f5d049ea526ebe5707444ea7ae96049b4e9602df1bccbdad27e, inventory(), nested_candidates, nested_marked, nested_index_paths): git ls-files -z --cached --sparse with /usr/bin/git, -c core.fsmonitor= (EMPTY: git < 2.36 runs any other value, false included, as a hook command found on PATH), GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null and GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0, over a private copy of the index plus sharedindex.* files (copied in the directory's own order); exit 129 alone (git's usage error: git < 2.35, as the image's 2.34.1, has no --sparse and exits so before reading the index) retries once without --sparse, and every other failure is final. The root .git is read first; then, at most SNAPSHOT_NESTED_INDEX_MAX of them, each repo-open folder (repoOpenMarkerRule) among projects/<repositoryId>/repository and repos/<handle>/<name>, taken as (layout, a, b) triples sorted component-wise by code point (so every projects/ folder before any repos/ one), skipping a folder whose name the codec could not archive (a backslash in a or b) before the binding is read; only a marked folder counts toward the cap. Each path and every prefix of it (prefixed with <layout>/<a>/<b>/ for a folder) is tracked. One inventory pass has two budgets, spent as the codec spends them: index bytes, one pool of SNAPSHOT_LIMIT_BYTES the root spends first and the folders then share (every copied byte, even by a read that then fails); ls-files output bytes, SNAPSHOT_INDEX_PATHS_BYTES for the root, then a second SNAPSHOT_INDEX_PATHS_BYTES the folders share (counted once git exits 0; output past the pool spends all of it). A folder's index that cannot be read, or that is past either pool, contributes nothing (as in the codec). A root index that cannot be read, or that is past either root pool, fails the codec's whole capture; the kernel then counts every cache-named entry (conservative). Where the kernel cannot decide as the codec would (an unreadable symlink target, a realpath that fails), it counts the entry (conservative, at most one header block plus PAX).
repoBudget.repoOpenMarkerRule: 1.0.2, 1.0.3 codec parity. A folder <layout>/<a>/<b> is a repo-open folder only when <layout>, <a>, <b> and .git are real directories (no symlink) and .git holds BINDING_FILE as a regular file of at most 4096 bytes whose content is strict UTF-8 (a byte-order mark is kept, so the JSON is refused) and parses as a JSON object with v === 1 (not a boolean, not a string). repos/<handle>/<name>: handle === <handle> and name === <name>; other keys are allowed. projects/<repositoryId>/repository (1.0.3 codec parity): exactly the five keys v, repositoryId, handle, name and gitHost, repositoryId === <repositoryId> (the directory's own name, whatever it is) and handle and name strings. The kernel writes that file into every folder it places (section 9.4 step 4), with exactly those five keys. The codec reads a nested index only for such a folder, so a workspace with no repo-open folder and no top-level STAGING_ROOT_NAME node (section 9.8 item 1, which a988f28c archived) checkpoints byte-identically to the a988f28c codec; the kernel's tracked set uses the same predicate. Known JSON-dialect differences, for bindings a guest writes itself (the kernel never does): the codec's Python json accepts NaN, Infinity and -Infinity, which JSON.parse refuses, and refuses nesting past Python's recursion limit (about 1000 levels on the image's Python 3.10), which JSON.parse accepts.
repoBudget.workspaceCasesRule: Each case lists every entry under the root (type file, dir, symlink or fifo), the paths each index lists (key '' is the root index, otherwise the folder), and the binding content of each folder that has one. expectArchived is the set of entry names the codec would archive under workspaceRule; expectTarBytes and expectEntries are their sums; expectOk is the verdict with the case's staged side. Lane tests build each case on a real filesystem with real git indexes (git adds its own files under each .git, which tests exclude from the comparison) and compare the kernel's archived names and verdict.

workspaceCases.case: untracked cache-named entries outside .git never count, whatever their type (one dependency install no longer refuses every open)
the same bytes in an ordinary directory count
a tracked dist inside a repo-open folder (binding present) counts; its untracked node_modules does not
the same tracked dist in a repos/<handle>/<name> clone without the binding does not count: the codec reads no index there, exactly as at a988f28c
a binding whose name differs from its folder, or whose v is not 1, marks nothing
a root-index tracked dist counts (a workspace that is itself a repository); its untracked node_modules does not
top-level internal names and the staging node never count; the same names deeper are ordinary content
cache names inside a .git path count; absolute, escaping and backslash names and FIFOs do not
1.0.3 codec parity: a tracked dist inside a bound projects/<repositoryId>/repository counts; the same layout with a four-key binding marks nothing, so its tracked dist does not count

cases.note: 80,000 empty files cost 40,960,000 tar bytes although their raw size is 0

phases.prepare: outside the persistence tail and outside withRuntimeMutation (holds neither); network allowed; writes only under <root>/.ezil-staging/<uuid> and /run/ezil. First removes every <root>/.ezil-staging/<u>, /run/ezil/requests/<u>.json and /run/ezil/git/incoming/<u>.json whose <u> is not in the request's inflight list.
phases.commit: inside the persistence tail (never withRuntimeMutation); no network; binding check, rename(2) into place, binding file, credential keys, grant install; releases the lock it owns on every outcome as its last act
phases.refresh: no tail; installs the grant and rewrites the /run/ezil/bin files only
phases.release: outside the tail; idempotent; removes this request's staging dir, the lock only when its owner file holds this request's uuid, the grant file only when the repository folder is absent, then this request's request and incoming files. Run by the Worker after every open and refresh outcome (section 8 step 11), including the busy path after tail acquire.

kernel.requestKeysRule: Strict: a request file with any key outside requestKeys plus optionalRequestKeys (1.0.3), any missing requestKeys key, a class outside constants REPO_OPEN_CLASSES, a gitHost other than REPO_OPEN_CLASS_GIT_HOSTS[class] (class absent = personal; class project: REPO_OPEN_PROJECT_GIT_HOSTS), a non-null path with class assessment (1.0.3 E1-6: its editor root is always the wrapper, assessment.layoutRule), a class project request whose gitHost is outside constants REPO_OPEN_PROJECT_GIT_HOSTS or whose path is non-null (1.0.4, project.rule), or a phase outside phases, is refused with workspace_failed before any filesystem or network action. inflight is the Worker in-flight map's uuids for this sandbox at the time the request is written (this request's uuid included).
kernel.lockRule: prepare (repository folder absent) takes LOCK_TEMPLATE with mkdir and writes this request's uuid to LOCK_OWNER_TEMPLATE. An existing lock is live only when its owner uuid is in the request's inflight list and it is younger than LOCK_STALE_MS; otherwise it is stale and prepare removes it and takes it. Released by commit on every outcome, by release, and by prepare itself on failure.
kernel.testSeam: The kernel module exports runKernel(phase, requestPath, testOptions). testOptions = { sslCAInfo, proxy } adds -c http.sslCAInfo=<file> -c http.proxy=<loopback CONNECT proxy> to every git command so tests reach a loopback TLS gateway that presents git-preview.ezil.work (and, from 1.0.3, git-qa.ezil.work for class assessment) under a test CA. The CLI entry (node <kernel> <phase> <request>, the only thing the Worker runs) passes no testOptions and has no other input channel: it reads no environment variable, and a request file carrying any test key is refused by requestKeysRule. Hosts, helper checks and allow-lists stay the class table's hosts (constants REPO_OPEN_CLASS_GIT_HOSTS).

gitEnv.rule: 1.0.3 (r56 review and its recheck). The whole environment of every git child the kernel starts through runGit (prepare, commit, refresh, release and the assessment reads), both classes: nothing is inherited, and git's own configuration sources are closed. GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 keeps /etc/gitconfig out, GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null keeps $HOME/.gitconfig and (git >= 2.32) the XDG config out, and XDG_CONFIG_HOME names a path that cannot exist (below a character device), so git also finds none of its XDG files ($XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config, ignore, attributes). GIT_ATTR_NOSYSTEM=1 keeps the system attributes file (/etc/gitattributes) out of checkout and the reads. GIT_TEMPLATE_DIR is empty, so git init (both gitInitCommands forms) copies no template directory (/usr/share/git-core/templates: its config, info/exclude and hooks) into .git. HOME names a path that cannot exist, so libcurl (inside git) reads no $HOME/.netrc; HOME is set, never unset, because without HOME libcurl reads the .netrc of the passwd home. A value guest root plants in any of those places (http.proxy, http.<url>.proxy, url.<base>.insteadOf, credential.helper, include.path, core.excludesFile, an eol or filter attribute, a template config or info/exclude, a netrc login, ...) never reaches ls-remote, fetch, checkout or the reads. Nothing in the kernel relies on any of them: the credential helper and every other key are written repo-locally (gitConfig, section 9.5) or passed with -c. Not closed (trust): the programs, shared libraries and other system files git and libcurl use (PATH, the CA store, the resolver configuration and /etc/hosts), which guest root can replace or rewrite as it can replace git itself. The assessment reads add hardenedRead.env on top (GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL repeated). The kernel's index read is no runGit child: it runs the snapshot codec's own binary and environment in a throwaway git dir (repoBudget.workspaceRule).

assessment.rule: 1.0.3. A request with class assessment (git host constants GIT_ASSESSMENT_HOST) differs from personal in these ways only. (1) Layout and fresh wrapper (E1-6, layoutRule): the clone F is <root>/projects/<repositoryId>/repository inside the wrapper W = <root>/projects/<repositoryId>, the editor root; path must be null (requestKeysRule). Prepare refuses with folder_conflict, before any action, when W exists in any form (lstat: a directory, a file, a symlink, a dangling symlink), and with workspace_failed when <root>/projects exists but is not a real directory; commit refuses the same way when W (or a bad <root>/projects) appeared after prepare (the lock is released, staging stays for release). Right after the rename commit re-checks the placement (layoutRule) and answers workspace_failed when it does not hold. There is no existing state, so a tree staged before the attempt can never satisfy readiness. These are in-guest checks that guest root under identity A can defeat (layoutRule scope, trust). (2) Exact branch: prepare checks out defaultBranch, never the remote HEAD's branch; a non-empty remote without refs/heads/<defaultBranch> is repository_unavailable, refused before the fetch (an empty remote is initialized_empty on defaultBranch, as for personal). (3) The commit answer for open carries resultOpenKeys (exact, in this order) with head, clean and remote, read by hardenedRead in the staging directory BEFORE the rename, all reads within one readBudgetMs; a read that fails (workspace_failed), a remote that is not ASSESSMENT_REMOTE_TEMPLATE (remoteRule, workspace_failed) or a read with no time left (workspace_busy) places no folder, so the open stays a fresh open. No git runs after the rename. folder and openFolder are W, pathNotFound is false. (4) An assessment commit that does not answer ok (it placed no folder, or its placement re-check failed) removes the grant file when this request still owns the lock (its own prepare installed that grant), never when another request does, then releases the lock. refresh and release locate F under W (layoutRule). Class personal (or absent) is unchanged: its folder is REPO_DIR_TEMPLATE and its answers carry kernel.resultOpenKeys only. The prepare answer keeps kernel.resultOpenKeys for both classes (callers read only ok and errorCode from it); for class assessment its folder and openFolder are W.
assessment.layoutRule: 1.0.3 E1-6. Class assessment: the wrapper W = <root>/ASSESSMENT_DIR_TEMPLATE (repositoryId is the request's lowercase UUID) is what the editor opens; the clone F = W/ASSESSMENT_CLONE_DIR_NAME (the OS open-project layout, worker/src/repo-open.ts REPO_OPEN_NESTED_DIR), so no file of the repository sits at the editor root. <root>/projects is looked up with lstat and must be a real directory when it exists (a symlink the kernel sees there is never followed), else workspace_failed; commit creates it when absent exactly as it creates <root>/repos (mode 0755, the kernel's uid). A fresh W is enforced by the kernel's checks: anything at W (lstat) refuses prepare and commit with folder_conflict; commit creates W with mkdir (EEXIST = folder_conflict), then rename(2)s staging to F; if the rename fails, commit removes W with rmdir (it is empty; a W that is no longer empty is left alone) and answers workspace_failed, so no folder is placed and the open stays retryable. Right after the rename commit re-checks the placement: the root is still a real directory that is its own realpath, <root>/projects, W and F are real directories (lstat, never followed) and W holds exactly one entry, ASSESSMENT_CLONE_DIR_NAME. Anything else is workspace_failed: the clone stays where the rename put it, so a re-open is refused as after a commit timeout, and the grant is removed (rule (4)). No git runs for the re-check. A commit killed between mkdir(W) and the rename (the host's commit timer) leaves an empty W, and every later open of that repositoryId answers folder_conflict; the window is two adjacent synchronous syscalls, recorded and not handled. Scope (E1-6 review): these are the kernel's own checks, observed in the guest at the moments it makes them. They keep the repository's own content (its .vscode, tasks and MCP files sit in F, below W) and any tree staged in the workspace before the attempt away from the editor root. They do not hold against guest root under identity A, who can add to or replace W, <root>/projects or F at any time: between mkdir(W) and the rename, between the re-check and the answer, and after placement (trust). refresh and release locate F only through real directories: refresh answers folder_conflict when <root>/projects or W exists but is not a real directory, or when F exists without this binding; release counts F as absent (and removes the grant) unless <root>/projects and W are real directories and F exists. The budget's staged side counts F's entries under their final names (projects/<repositoryId>/repository/...) plus projects and projects/<repositoryId> when absent. Class personal keeps F = <root>/REPO_DIR_TEMPLATE, byte-identical.
assessment.headRule: The 40-lowercase-hex commit id HEAD resolves to (git rev-parse --verify -q 'HEAD^{commit}', whose stdout must be exactly 40 hex and a newline). null only when that fails, git rev-parse --verify -q HEAD fails too (HEAD names no object at all), and git symbolic-ref -q HEAD succeeds with a refs/heads/ name (an unborn branch: an empty repository). Any other outcome is workspace_failed: HEAD detached at a missing commit, a branch that names a tree or another non-commit, a symbolic ref outside refs/heads/ (refs/tags/missing, refs/remotes/origin/missing). A read with no time left in readBudgetMs, or killed at its timeout, is workspace_busy. empty === (head === null), and state is initialized_empty exactly when head is null.
assessment.cleanRule: true exactly when git status --porcelain=v1 --untracked-files=all exits 0 and prints nothing (ignored files are not listed). A non-zero exit is workspace_failed; a timeout is workspace_busy.
assessment.remoteRule: 1.0.3 E1-6. remote is constants ASSESSMENT_REMOTE_TEMPLATE for the request's handle and name, read back in the staging directory BEFORE the rename with hardenedRead, inside the same readBudgetMs: git config --get-all remote.origin.url, without --local, so a value added through include.path is seen too (git 2.34.1 and 2.43 list it; --local would hide it). It must exit 0 and print exactly one line equal to the expected URL; anything else (no value, two values, another host, handle or name, userinfo) is workspace_failed and places no folder; a read with no time left is workspace_busy. remote is the configured remote.origin.url, not the effective fetch or push target: remote.origin.pushurl, url.<base>.insteadOf and url.<base>.pushInsteadOf are not read, and only guest root can set them (the staged .git/config is written by the kernel, and nothing fetched from the git host changes it). Like head and clean it is in-guest evidence (trust).

hardenedRead.rule: Every head, clean and remote read runs with the kernel's cleared environment plus env, the kernel's -c list (which includes config) and globalOptions, cwd the staging directory, each read bounded by the LOCAL git timeout and by the time left in readBudgetMs. core.fsmonitor is set to the EMPTY value, which turns fsmonitor off on every git: git < 2.36 (the sandbox image's 2.34.1) reads the value false as a hook command and runs the PATH's false; every kernel git command carries the same setting. No optional lock is taken, so a read killed at its timeout never leaves .git/index.lock (which would abort the workspace export capture). These settings keep the kernel's own environment from adding anything; they do not make the repository's own state trustworthy (trust).

assessment.trust: head, clean, remote and the layout (W, <root>/projects and F; layoutRule) are in-guest evidence, not proof. The kernel and git run as uid 0 in the guest, and so do code-server and the terminal on AWS (the desktop's runc process is uid 0). Under identity A (the candidate is the owner of the existing computer) guest root can, between prepare and commit or at any other time: add a filter driver to the staged .git/config with a matching .git/info/attributes entry (it runs during status and can hide a change); set core.worktree, .git/info/exclude, or the index's skip-worktree or assume-unchanged bits so that status prints nothing for a dirty tree; plant programs on the reads' PATH; set remote.origin.pushurl, url.<base>.insteadOf or url.<base>.pushInsteadOf so that fetch and push go elsewhere while remote.origin.url reads back as expected; put files into W (a .vscode/tasks.json that runs on folder open, say), or replace W, F or <root>/projects with a symlink outside <root>, between the kernel's mkdir(W), its rename and its placement re-check, or after placement; or replace git or node. hardenedRead and gitEnv keep out only what the kernel's own environment would add: git's own configuration sources (system, global and XDG config, the XDG ignore and attributes files, the system attributes file, the template directory, and files under HOME such as .netrc; no kernel git reads any of them since the r56 review and its recheck), hooks, fsmonitor, a pager and repository discovery above the directory. They do not cover the programs, libraries and other system files git and libcurl use (PATH, the CA store, the resolver configuration and /etc/hosts): guest root can replace or rewrite those, as it can replace git, and so steer prepare's network phase and the reads. The placement re-check sees only its own moment. A consumer records readiness from head, clean and remote as in-candidate-container evidence, and never treats the editor root's content as platform-controlled; a proof needs a read outside the guest.
assessment.editorRootRule: 1.0.3 E1-6: kernel-enforced against the repository's content and against trees staged before the attempt; in-guest evidence against guest root under identity A (trust). It replaces the earlier consumer precondition for those two only: no consumer may treat W's content as platform-controlled. The editor root is the wrapper W (layoutRule), never F, because code-server reads runnable config (.vscode, tasks, MCP and the like) from the root of the folder it opens. The kernel's checks establish that W did not exist in any form when prepare and commit looked (lstat) and that right after the rename it held exactly one entry, ASSESSMENT_CLONE_DIR_NAME, under real directories (layoutRule), so neither the repository's content nor a tree staged before the attempt sits at the editor root. Guest root can still add to W, or redirect W or <root>/projects outside <root>, at any time; what Code then opens is the candidate's own doing, never the platform's; every assessment answer names W as folder and openFolder, and the consumer refuses any other folder. Path collision: the live open-project flow (worker/src/repo-open.ts REPO_OPEN_NESTED_DIR) places its own clones at the same <root>/projects/<repositoryId>/repository. In one workspace an assessment answers folder_conflict for a repositoryId open-project already placed (never adopted); what open-project does with a W an assessment placed is open-project's own rule, not this contract's. A personal folder <root>/repos/<handle>/<name> no longer blocks the assessment of the same <handle>/<name> (the folders differ). Grants and locks stay keyed by handle and name for both classes (GRANT_FILE_TEMPLATE, LOCK_TEMPLATE; the helper is unchanged): a personal and an assessment repository with the same handle and name share one lock and one grant slot, so an install by either replaces the other's grant (the helper then refuses the other's host until its next refresh), and a release whose own F is absent removes the shared grant. That is a liveness limit, never an adoption.

project.rule: 1.0.4. A request with class project differs from class assessment in these ways only. (1) Host: gitHost is one of constants REPO_OPEN_PROJECT_GIT_HOSTS (the route passes the deployment's one; the kernel accepts either). (2) Marker: after writeBinding, prepare writes .git/PROJECT_MARKER_FILE in the staging clone with exactly PROJECT_MARKER_CONTENT (O_EXCL, a regular file); commit refuses a staged folder without it. The binding stays the 5-key BINDING_FILE, so the codec's repoOpenMarkerRule and codecTracked are unchanged, and the snapshot carries the marker with the rest of .git. (3) Reopen: an existing W whose only entry is a real directory F that is bound to this request (binding) AND marked is answered existing, read-only, with no network: folder = openFolder = W, pathNotFound false, branch defaultBranch, empty false; its commit installs the new grant (refresh semantics) and never moves or rewrites F. Anything else at W (absent parent chain aside) is folder_conflict: an assessment-placed W (unmarked) is never adopted, and an assessment request never adopts a project W (assessment adopts nothing). (4) Answer: the 7-key resultOpenKeys, states cloned | initialized_empty | existing; no head, clean or remote; branch per branchRule. (5) Grant: as assessment, removed only when this request placed nothing and did not reopen.
project.layoutRule: 1.0.4. As kernel.assessment.layoutRule: W = <root>/ASSESSMENT_DIR_TEMPLATE, F = W/ASSESSMENT_CLONE_DIR_NAME, no symlink anywhere on <root>/projects/W/F (lstat; never followed), the parent chain refused with workspace_failed, a foreign W with folder_conflict. The editor root is W.
project.markerRule: 1.0.4. projectMarked(F) holds exactly when F/.git/PROJECT_MARKER_FILE is lstat'd as a regular file (never a symlink) whose bytes are exactly PROJECT_MARKER_CONTENT. A tampered, symlinked, extended or missing marker makes an existing W folder_conflict for class project; a marker never makes a W adoptable for class assessment.
project.branchRule: 1.0.4. A fresh placement (cloned, initialized_empty) checks out exactly defaultBranch, as assessment (r56): a non-empty remote without defaultBranch is repository_unavailable; an empty remote initializes defaultBranch unborn. An existing reopen names the folder's current branch (HEAD's symbolic ref, as a personal reopen; defaultBranch when HEAD is detached): the Creator's own branch work is never forced back, and the Worker and host accept any valid branch for state existing only.
project.twoPushRule: 1.0.4 T-2PUSH-K. After an open, git push succeeds with the installed grant; once the grant's expiresAt is inside the helper's skew it is refused (HELPER_HINT_EXPIRED) without reaching the server; a refresh with a DIFFERENT token installs it (the old token revoked at the server) and the next push succeeds, while the working tree, the index and HEAD are unchanged by the refresh and the refresh makes no network request.

awsOutcomeOrigin.rule: 1.0.3 (r56 review, the consumer rule of slot1 D1). The origin of every repo-open outcome a consumer can see on the AWS path (worker/src/aws-repo-open.ts in front of infra/host-agent/lib/ezil_host/repo_open.py): the refusal codes (workerResponses.refusals) and the ok states (okOpen and okRefresh). worker: decided by the Worker relay or its calling route before or without the guest. host: decided by the host agent outside the guest (admission, deadlines, cgroup and runc checks, the job store, the sanitizer). guest: produced by, or derivable from, the kernel running inside the candidate's computer (its last stdout line, or its behaviour: a stall, a failing exec, a stopped desktop), and therefore forgeable by guest root once the grant is installed. A code produced on several paths carries every origin, joined with | in the order of values; paths names one path per origin, each prefixed with its origin. running (a start or poll step, never final) is decided by the worker (it could not tell) or the host (its job store). Guest root can delay the final outcome within the host's deadline, and under identity A the owner can keep it from ever becoming final: a control-plane stop or restart of the computer after the grant, or an idle stop, ends the host agent and the results it holds in memory, and from then on a poll answers running (aws-repo-open.ts: an awsControlTarget Response at a poll is running, and so is an assessment poll whose until has passed), so running may never become final.
awsOutcomeOrigin.consumerRule: Founder 32d1100d with slot1 r63–r65 (C-CLOCK2; it replaces the withdrawn r61 clock, which began at the grant). The consumer (f6a67dd0's orchestrator) runs every assessment attempt in three phases. PREPARE, before the recorded start: an admission before START binds identity only; no candidate has computer access (Code, desktop, terminal, preview), the task or a usable write grant. The open runs on the trusted path (the Worker relay, the host op and the sha-pinned kernel) with a grant of scope read (grantFile scope; the kernel accepts read and write); every PREPARE outcome, whatever its origin, is non-consuming. The host never reads /workspace (the A2h boundary), so on AWS the checkout's content (head, clean, remote and branch) is read only by the kernel inside the guest. Readiness is attested by the host job store's result for this attempt's open, the host epoch unchanged since that open, Works' starter-SHA pin equal to head, and the pre-admission precondition: the guest's state is fresh for this attempt, that is a fresh data volume (upper, /workspace, profiles) claimed from the pinned image in PREPARE before the open, with the AMI, instance and both volume ids from AWS API receipts (F-SEAT-RESET (A), r64 and r65; a new instance or a new root volume alone keeps the data volume and clears nothing), and no candidate or owner has reached the guest since that volume was attached. Without that precondition the attempt is not ready (a non-consuming platform failure) and is never started; a candidate who can reach the guest before START is a gate defect. START is one atomic consumer transaction: countdown start, immutable deadline, task release, and the candidate's computer access and write grant. The grant cannot be minted inside it, and it reaches the computer only by op refresh with scope write, an exec in the guest, in one of two orders (f6a67dd0 decides): (i) r63 CK-3: Works mints it before START, idempotent per attempt and undelivered; START commits; then the brief, the access and the grant are delivered, and a delivery failure that no AWS API record proves to be provider loss consumes the attempt; (ii) r64: minted and delivered as the last PREPARE step, only while the seat is bound, fresh and unreachable, expiring by S+G+D and revoked at E1 or a no-show; START records it, remote services admit only the committed START epoch, and a delivery failure aborts PREPARE, non-consuming. Either way an interrupted delivery re-delivers the same grant, never a second, and never moves the deadline. AFTER START, every outcome the candidate can cause is consuming and never extends the deadline: any outcome whose origin includes guest, and any worker- or host-origin outcome the candidate can induce (an instance-initiated shutdown, an instance status-check failure, an idle stop from inactivity; a stop or restart where the candidate controls the computer). Only a provider loss proven from the AWS API (r63 CK-2: an EC2 Server.* state reason, a failed system status check or an AWS Health event; never the guest or the instance itself) is non-consuming. Restarts are capped, and no restart reopens the clock. The owner notes on workspace_unsupported, runtime_not_running and workspace_not_ready assume identity A (the candidate owns the computer); with placement on Creator or company capacity an owner's stop is not the candidate's act, and the consumer classifies it. The success fields head, clean, remote and branch, and the wrapper rules (kernel.assessment.layoutRule, editorRootRule), are in-guest evidence only (kernel.assessment.trust).

productionOs.rule: 1.0.2. Production OS is OS_PRODUCTION_APP_ORIGIN (Vercel project ezil-os-preview; EZiL-OS .github/scripts/release-state.mjs `canonical`, moved from os.ezil.org on 2026-10-18). OS_LANDING_ORIGIN (os.ezil.org) is the static landing Worker, not an OS app, and is probed only as the landing page. G-READ reads the production AUTH0_CLIENT_ID of os.ezil.work and of every other live OS app deployment (ids only). X1 P3 decides with pinGate over the two pins and the ids G-READ read; outcomes in pinGateOrder, first match wins. production_client_unlisted means a contract bump that adds the read id to PRODUCTION_AUTH0_CLIENTS (vectors, OS app/src/server/repo-open/targets.ts, Works apps/api/src/deployment.ts, every consumer copy re-seeded) must land first; the pin commit follows it and pinGate is rerun.

placeholderClientIds.about: Placeholders standing for ids G-READ has not read yet. They are not Auth0 ids and never reach code.

productionOs.pinGateRule: Symbols resolve through fixtures.clientIds, then productionOs.placeholderClientIds; 'UNPINNED' and '' are literal. production_clients_unread: G-READ returned no production OS client id. pin_ineffective: either pin is UNPINNED or empty. pin_is_production: either pin equals a PRODUCTION_AUTH0_CLIENTS id or any id G-READ read. pins_equal: the two pins are equal. production_client_unlisted: some id G-READ read is not in PRODUCTION_AUTH0_CLIENTS. pin: otherwise.

workerExec.timeoutRule: 1.0.2. Sandbox SDK 0.12.1 does not throw when a sessionless exec reaches its timeout: the container kills the process tree and the call returns a normal result with exitCode 124 and stderr 'Command timed out after <N>ms'. The Worker treats an exec result as a timeout when exitCode === 124 AND (elapsedMs >= timeoutMs - 500 OR stderr matches /Command timed out after \d+ms\s*$/). The kernel only ever exits 0 or 2. A thrown exec is a timeout only when elapsedMs >= timeoutMs - 500. A timeout is never parsed as a kernel answer; its refusal is timeoutErrorByStep.

timeoutCases.case: the SDK message with a trailing newline, before the full timeout elapsed on the Worker clock
exit 124 at the full timeout without the message
a kernel refusal (exit 2) at the full timeout
the message with another exit code
the message not at the end of stderr, early

workerExec.timeoutErrorNote: commit maps to workspace_busy since 1.0.2 (it was workspace_failed): the rename may already have happened, and the next open is idempotent (existing) or re-clones after release. That holds for class personal only: class assessment uses assessment.timeoutErrorByStep (1.0.3). release falls back to removing exactly this request's staging, request and incoming files (section 8 step 11).

assessment.rule: 1.0.3. For class assessment, workspace_busy always means that this job placed no folder, so the same open may be started again. The kernel guarantees it: an assessment commit reads head and clean before its rename and runs no git after it, and every kernel workspace_busy comes before the rename. A commit exec that times out, or whose cleanup is not confirmed before its answer exists, may have renamed. It answers workspace_failed, because an assessment re-open could only answer folder_conflict (the AWS host: repo_open.py; the Cloudflare exec path: this map). On AWS, once the host has admitted a start, the caller polls that same job until done and never starts it again (a finished result stays readable for the host's JOB_TTL, 600 s, and is never evicted earlier: r56 D3, a host whose result store already holds JOBS_MAX unexpired results refuses a new start with workspace_busy before admitting it). A poll whose own until has passed sends nothing and reports running. The one-call composition (handleAwsRepoOpen) answers workspace_failed when its deadline passes after the start, because the job's outcome is unknown and the caller cannot poll it.

stopped.when: the tombstone is set or the container is not running

transition.when: a runtime transition is in flight (restartDesktopStack, the migration fence) while the container runs
transition.release: runs: its guarded exec queues behind withRuntimeMutation and runs once the transition ends (if a transition is still in flight then, the guard skips it like a stop)

workerExec.inflightJoinRule: 1.0.2. A request joins a running one only when handle/name, op AND path are equal (null equals null). Any other request on the same handle/name, and any open while another open runs in the sandbox, is workspace_busy, which the wake loop retries, so a second open with another path gets its own openFolder. A joiner's own grant is not installed: the installed grant is the joined request's, minted at most one Worker deadline earlier, so the joiner's gitAccessExpiresAt can be later than the installed grant's expiry by about that much; the refresh lead (REFRESH_LEAD_MS) exceeds it (accepted).

routeGate.rule: 1.0.2. POST /sandbox/<name>/repo-open is mounted only when the Worker's existing var EZIL_AI_GATEWAY_URL equals stagingValue (os-staging's own Gateway, which production never uses: I6). Any other or missing value leaves the route unmounted, so the request falls through, before its body is read or its signature checked, to the Worker's generic 404 for an undeclared path (body {"ok":false,"error":"not_found"}: the entry's json() keeps only the public code of 'not_found: POST <path>'), exactly as a988f28c answers that path. No env var is added.

imageInputs.rule: 1.0.2. No repo-open source path is a CI image input (.github/workflows/preview.yml env IMAGE_INPUTS): a change under an image input sets image_changed, rebuilds the sandbox image and deploys the Worker with --containers-rollout immediate, which recycles every live computer. The generator is a dev-time tool in worker/tools/ (it was in worker/scripts/, an image input, before 1.0.2); the kernel and helper reach a computer only as bytes in the Worker bundle (section 8 step 7). X1 P6 deploys the staging Worker with --containers-rollout none after proving git diff --name-only <live source> <deploy sha> -- <IMAGE_INPUTS> is empty.

gatewayExtract.about: EZiL CLI is a public repository, so it commits this reduced extract instead of the full vectors: no database, Supabase or preview IP hosts. check.mjs builds it deterministically from the canonical vectors (JSON.stringify(extract, null, 2) + newline, keys in the order below) and prints its sha256, which is pinned in README-universe-repo-open.md. Write it with: node docs/contracts/universe-repo-open-v1.check.mjs --emit-gateway-extract > <EZiL CLI>/contracts/universe-repo-open-v1.gateway.json

awsProject.rule: 1.0.4. The AWS relay sends a class project start only after BOTH gates the integrating route supplies answer exactly true for THIS computer: projectCapable (the host's agent and kernel know class project: an AMI after 1.0.30 carrying the A2h repo-open op and this kernel) and computerFree (the computer is the Creator's own and is not bound to an assessment attempt; the assessment policy's answer). A gate that is absent, answers anything but true, or throws is workspace_unsupported with no edge call. Nothing provisions compute; EZiL ID alone is never checkout proof (the grant comes from Works, OS-scoped, W2/W3).
awsProject.ami1030: AMI 1.0.30 (host agent 7b95bcd9) has no repo-open op: start answers 404, so class project there is workspace_unsupported. An A2h host whose class table predates 1.0.4 answers 409 repo_open_invalid: also workspace_unsupported. Neither is retried.
